newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets $360 mln rail assets value. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets $360 mln rail assets value. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]

text.p: The value of the assets of the Pacific-North railroad being privatized is $360 million, Communications and Transport ministry privatization coordinator Jorge Silberstein said on Thursday.

"The value of the assets of the Pacific-North is $360 million," he said at a press conference. This amount is not necessarily the official minimum bid the government sets for the concession winner to operate the railroad.
Only one consortia is bidding for the railway, Mexico's largest with 3,875 miles (6,200 kilometers) of rail.

The sole bid is composed of mining company Grupo Mexico, Mexican builder Empresas ICA and U.S. Union Pacific. The amount bidded for the rail and the decision on if the group will win the concession will be announced on June 26.

Silberstein did not say if the value determined for the assets includes the Chihuahua-Pacifico line, known as the Copper Canyon. A month ago the government set the price for the track at 253.5 million pesos or about $31.89 million.

The more coveted Northeast railway concession was sold last December for $1.4 million, at least twice the value of the assets and the government's minimum bid. The winning consortium was composed of Transportacion Maritima Mexicana and Kansas City Southern Industries
